articles.body:
Biggest injury concerns for Week 10

Players in Germany

Amon-Ra St. Brown, WR, Lions (ribs): The "Sun God" was limited at practice this week and is listed as questionable but appears likely to play in Week 10. He played through the injury last week and surpassed 16 fantasy points. St. Brown, who is a German citizen, will look to put on a show.

A.J. Brown, WR, Patriots (ankle/knee): Brown has been limited at practice this week and is questionable for Week 10. Brown averaged eight targets per game for the two times that he played on over 75% of snaps. Given all the missed time, he brings some risk. Still, if he suits up, fantasy managers should take the chance as he has a fantastic matchup against the Lions, who have allowed the fourth-most WR fantasy PPG.

Rhamondre Stevenson, RB, Patriots (knee): Stevenson was able to return in a limited fashion after missing practice to start the week. He is listed as questionable for Sunday. He has a tough matchup against the Lions, who have allowed the second-fewest fantasy PPG. They rank bottom six in rushing touchdowns and rushing yards per game allowed to RBs. He would be a risky flex option if he suits up. If he sits, Corey Kiner is the next man up. He would see volume, which is enough to have him in the flex range, but he should ideally be avoided if possible.

Hunter Henry, TE, Patriots (foot): Henry has been limited at practice this week but does not currently carry an injury designation for Week 10. That means he is expected to play. Henry is a TE1 worth starting against the Lions, who have allowed the most yards, touchdowns and fantasy points to tight ends.

Don't forget to check these out: Mike Clay's Playbook | Week 10 Buzz 

Week 10 Rankings | Matchup rankings for Week 10

Official Sunday inactives should begin coming in approximately 90 minutes before the scheduled kickoff times: around 11:30 a.m. ET for the early games and 2:30 p.m. ET for the late-afternoon games.

Refresh often for the latest information.

Players with early starts

Harold Fannin Jr., TE, Browns (groin): While Fannin was limited at practice this week, he has been removed from Cleveland's injury report and will play in Week 10. The Texans' defense is tough on tight ends, having allowed the fourth-fewest fantasy PPG to the position. Still, consider Fannin to be a TE1 this week in a game where the Browns might be trailing and needing to throw.

Denzel Boston, WR, Browns (toe): Boston missed practice on Thursday before returning Friday. He is questionable for Week 10, but HC Todd Monken said on Friday that Boston is "trending in the right direction." On paper, Boston has a favorable matchup against the Texans, although they have been tougher as of late. He is in the WR3/flex range. If he were to sit, KC Concepcion gets the biggest boost and would be in a similar range as Boston. Fannin, albeit in a tough matchup, would also likely see a few more targets.

articles.headline: Seahawks are hurting with injuries, but two players will return vs. Raiders
articles.description: QB Drew Lock will start again for Darnold. LB Uchenna Nwosu and WR Rashid Shaheed will return to the field in Las Vegas.
articles.headlineJa: シーホークスは負傷者に苦しむも、レイダース戦で2人の選手が復帰
articles.descriptionJa: QBドリュー・ロックが再びダーノルドに代わって先発。LBウチェンナ・ヌウォスとWRラシード・シャヒードがラスベガスでの試合に復帰する。
articles.body:
RENTON, Wash. - Seattle Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Drew Lock had a good week of practice as he prepares to fill in again for Sam Darnold on Sunday against the 4-5 Las Vegas Raiders (4:05 p.m. ET, CBS) -- this time despite a pair of ailments of his own.

Lock was already dealing with an injury to his right elbow when he hurt his oblique last Sunday in Seattle's 17-3 win over the Arizona Cardinals. He was again limited in practice all week, as has been the case since the start of Week 6.

"Similar cadence in workload in terms of last week," Macdonald said Friday. "It's good to have done it and gotten through the week well. I know he's confident and optimistic, so we're in good shape."

In addition to Darnold (quad, rib) and left guard Quenton Nelson (knee) -- whom Macdonald had ruled out earlier in the week -- the Seahawks will be without defensive tackle Leonard Williams (stinger) and left tackle Charles Cross (ankle) again Sunday.

They'll get outside linebacker Uchenna Nwosu (ankle) and wide receiver/kick returner Rashid Shaheed (knee) back against the Raiders after each missed the past two games. Defensive tackle Jarran Reed will play Sunday after missing two days this week to tend to a personal matter.

Lock said Thursday that he was feeling good, and that his oblique injury wasn't impacting his throwing all that much. It's on his right side, which Lock said is "way better" for a right-handed quatrerback than a left oblique injury, which caused him to miss two weeks during the preseason when he was with the New York Giants in 2024.

"I feel like we did a great job handling the week last week, and here we are, we've just got a little something added to it, and I think we're doing the same," Lock said. "We're doing a great job getting ready."

Macdonald volunteered that No. 3 quarterback Jalen Milroe "has done a tremendous job" while taking reps with the Seahawks' No. 1 offense as the team continues to manage Lock's workload in practice.

Sunday's game will mark Lock's third start this season and the fourth time he's stepped in for Darnold, who hurt his glute on the fifth play of the opener, then suffered a cracked rib and a quad injury in Week 8.

Macdonald has said Darnold might be able to return for the Seahawks' game against the San Francisco 49ers in Week 12, following their bye.

"I see Sam progressing with his rehab," Macdonald said. "The guys are saying he's doing a great job and he's progressing. We'll take it a day and a week at a time."

Williams will miss his second straight game due to a stinger. He took part in pre-practice warmups on Wednesday and Thursday but was listed as a non-participant all week.

"It's more of a contact thing," Macdonald said. "So he's done a good job of staying in shape and staying fresh. He's in the meetings. He's doing all the Leo things. He's just not playing right now."

articles.descriptionJa: レアル・マドリードはバイエルン・ミュンヘンのスター、マイケル・オリーズへの関心を維持している。Transfer Talkが最新情報をお届けする。
articles.body:
Bayern Munich star Michael Olise is still being tailed by Real Madrid, while United States internationals Folarin Balogun and Alex Freeman could be following coach Mauricio Pochettino to Manchester United. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Real Madrid remain interested in Bayern Munich winger Michael Olise, after previously being linked with him during the summer, according to L'Equipe. The 24-year-old is reported to have multiple top clubs in Europe 'dreaming' of signing him next summer, when he will enter the final two years of his contract at the Allianz Arena. Olise scored in France's 3-1 Nations League defeat against Italy on Thursday.

- Manchester United have added United States duo Folarin Balogun and Alex Freeman to their list, TEAMtalk reports. Monaco striker Balogun, 25, and Villarreal defender Freeman, 22, are seen as two ideal candidates to land in January due to their familiarity with the USMNT coach Mauricio Pochettino. It was announced on Friday that Pochettino has agreed a deal to become the next manager at United and replace the fired Michael Carrick at Old Trafford. The Red Devils have been monitoring Freeman for some time, but could now step up their interest following his impressive performances under Pochettino for the USMNT. Balogun has said that he will look to seal a move away from Monaco in the next transfer window, having seen his proposed move to Everton fall through in the summer.

- Liverpool are keen on Brighton & Hove Albion defender Luka Vuskovic, Florian Plettenberg reports. The Reds are monitoring the 19-year-old regularly after placing him on their shortlist of options for next summer, and he could be seen as a potential long term successor to Virgil van Dijk, who is yet to sign an extension on his current deal which is set to expire in June. There is no release clause in Vuskovic's contract, with his transfer expected to require a proposal worth in the region of €100 million.

- Chelsea right back Malo Gusto is attracting interest from Manchester City and Manchester United, according to talkSPORT. Both clubs are keeping tabs on the situation of the 23-year-old, who has only made three starts in the Premier League this season. The Blues would demand an offer worth £75 million before agreeing to part ways with him, in a deal that could see Gusto reunite with former manager Enzo Maresca at the Etihad Stadium.

- Juventus are interested in Tottenham Hotspur's Destiny Udogie and Barcelona's Alejandro Balde as new left backs,according to Corriere dello Sport. Udogie, 23, has made just two starts in the Premier League this season as the second choice option to Andy Robertson, and he has been identified as a player that the Bianconeri could acquire to reinforce the left side of their defense in January. Balde, 23, has also struggled to garner first team minutes and is linked with an exit from Camp Nou.

articles.headline: Lakers' Austin Reaves day-to-day with left heel bruise
articles.description: Lakers guard Austin Reaves is considered day-to-day as he deals with a left heel bruise, coach JJ Redick said Friday.
articles.headlineJa: レイカーズのオースティン・リーブス、左かかとの打撲で日々の状態を確認
articles.descriptionJa: レイカーズのガード、オースティン・リーブスが左かかとの打撲を抱えており、日単位で状態を確認していると、JJ・レディック監督が金曜日に明らかにした。
articles.body:
EL SEGUNDO, Calif. -- Los Angeles Lakers guard Austin Reaves is considered day-to-day as he deals with a left heel bruise, coach JJ Redick said after practice Friday.

Reaves left L.A.'s 123-112 victory over the Milwaukee Bucks on Wednesday midway through the third quarter and did not return after landing awkwardly on his left foot after missing a contested fast-break dunk.

Reaves underwent X-rays at the arena Wednesday that came back clean. After seeing how Reaves was feeling Thursday morning once the Lakers returned to Los Angeles, the team determined that further medical imaging on the shooting guard's foot would not be necessary.

When Redick was asked if Reaves had suffered only a "minor" injury, considering the Lakers decided to forgo an MRI, the coach replied: "I would assume a day-to-day injury is minor, yeah."

Redick provided injury updates on three other Lakers players as well.

Luka Doncic, who turned his right ankle late in the win over the Bucks, "is fine," according to Redick.

"I think the expectation would be he's available," Redick said, referring to L.A.'s next game against the Phoenix Suns on Sunday.

Redick said backup guard Collin Sexton, who required stitches above his right eye after he and Bucks guard Ryan Rollins unintentionally head-butted one another Wednesday, was cleared of any concussion symptoms but is also considered day-to-day. 

Guard Quentin Grimes, who sprained the right pinkie on his shooting hand and missed the Lakers' past two games, participated in the live portion of practice Friday, Redick said.

Grimes said he jammed the finger in the Pistons game and taped it up for practice.

"The swelling has gone down a lot," Grimes said. "It's kind of feeling basically back to normal."

The Lakers, at 11-2, own the No. 1 record in the NBA. Redick used the three-day break in the schedule to "audit" the team. He said he had his analytics department prepare a 21-page presentation he used, along with a film session, to discuss L.A.'s defensive and offensive identities before practice Friday.

"It was good," forward Ziaire Williams said of the meeting. "A lot of good things and a lot of things to clean up. Being first in the West, with the stuff that they showed us, you would think we were almost last, you know? But yeah, for sure, got to keep us honest."

articles.headline: 49ers OT Williams, LB Greenlaw questionable, WR Evans out vs. Cowboys
articles.description: The 49ers are listing left tackle Trent Williams and linebacker Dre Greenlaw as questionable for Sunday's game against the Cowboys, while receiver Mike Evans has been ruled out.
articles.headlineJa: 49ersのOTウィリアムズとLBグリーンロウが出場不透明、WRエヴァンスはカウボーイズ戦を欠場
articles.descriptionJa: 49ersは、日曜日のカウボーイズ戦に向けてレフトタックルのトレント・ウィリアムズとラインバッカーのドレ・グリーンロウを出場不透明としており、レシーバーのマイク・エヴァンスは欠場が決定した。
articles.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- The San Francisco 49ers had two important additions to their injury report this week with left tackle Trent Williams (shoulder) and linebacker Dre Greenlaw (knee) now listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Dallas Cowboys.

According to coach Kyle Shanahan, Williams and Greenlaw suffered their injuries in Thursday's practice, with both players listed as limited for that day because of it. Greenlaw was again limited Friday, while Williams did not practice.

"Anytime you hurt your shoulder on a Thursday, it doesn't make you totally at ease," Shanahan said of Williams. "Sunday comes fast, but hopefully that's enough time for him to be all right."

If Williams is unable to play, the Niners will turn to swing tackle Vederian Lowe to step into the lineup. And if Greenlaw can't play, rookie Jaden Dugger will move into the weakside linebacker spot, according to Shanahan.

"Hopefully we'll have Dre on Sunday, but if we don't, next man up, and our next man's proven himself so far," Shanahan said.

Elsewhere on the injury report, wide receiver Mike Evans (Achilles) will miss his third straight game. He's the only Niner officially ruled out against the Cowboys as he continues to work his way through the tendinitis that flared up in Week 6 against the Washington Commanders.

Shanahan offered a bit more clarity Friday afternoon on when Evans could return, saying there's "a chance" for next week against the Minnesota Vikings but adding that he's "not sure yet."

"It's been going well," Shanahan said. "I'm sure if this was the last game or something, he'd be able to go out there. But we're just trying to make sure it fully heals so it doesn't act up again, but it's going in the right direction."

In addition to Williams and Greenlaw, all three of San Francisco's top cornerbacks -- Deommodore Lenoir (foot), Renardo Green (back) and Upton Stout (shoulder/neck) -- are questionable against the Cowboys.

So, too, are defensive tackle C.J. West (knee) and defensive back Nate Hobbs (adductor), both of whom are working their way back from injured reserve and could be activated Saturday.

Meanwhile, wide receiver Deebo Samuel, who has been out with a hamstring injury since Week 5, practiced all week and is cleared to return against the Cowboys.

"He had a good week, healthy," Shanahan said. "First week back, so he's still getting back into it, but [he] took care of himself real well while he was injured and had a good week."

articles.headline: Dejounte Murray wants trade from Pelicans; both sides working on resolution
articles.description: Pelicans guard Dejounte Murray wants a trade from the franchise, and his agent, Klutch Sports CEO Rich Paul, and team officials have started working on a resolution.
articles.headlineJa: デジョウンテ・マレーがペリカンズからのトレードを希望、双方が解決策を模索
articles.descriptionJa: ペリカンズのガード、デジョウンテ・マレーがチームからのトレードを希望しており、代理人のKlutch Sports CEOリッチ・ポールとチーム関係者が解決に向けた協議を開始した。
articles.body:
New Orleans Pelicans guard Dejounte Murray wants a trade from the franchise, and his agent, Klutch Sports CEO Rich Paul, and team officials have started working on a resolution.

"Today, Dejounte Murray's representatives informed us of his request to be traded," the Pelicans said in a statement Friday. "We will evaluate potential trade opportunities that are in the best interest of our organization."

Murray has made it clear to the organization that he is ready to play a key role in meaningful basketball elsewhere, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

The Pelicans are 4-8 to start the season and have lost four games in a row, including a 145-111 blowout at home to the Brooklyn Nets on Wednesday. Murray has been ruled out because of a left ankle sprain for Friday night's NBA Cup game against the Memphis Grizzlies.

After the latest game, Murray tweeted a response to an account that noted that the Pelicans are 3-0 without Murray in the lineup and 1-8 with him on the court: "From what's going on INSIDE, this sounds like someone hit you to say this! THE 'SABOTAGE' IS REAL!," the since-deleted tweet read.

Murray, 30, was acquired by the Pelicans in a June 2024 trade with the Atlanta Hawks, as New Orleans dealt two first-round picks, Dyson Daniels, Larry Nance Jr. and E.J. Liddell to Atlanta for him. Murray was coming off a 2023-24 season in which he averaged 22.5 points, 6.4 assists and 5.3 rebounds per game.

He has dealt with major injuries and played just 54 games over the past three seasons, however. He has averaged 16.6 points, 6.6 assists and 5.9 rebounds for the Pelicans, shooting just 41.9% from the floor. He broke a hand in the 2024 season opener and suffered a season-ending ruptured right Achilles tendon in January 2025. Murray is averaging just 13.4 points per game this season.

Murray, who made the All-Star team in 2022, is making $32.8 million this season and has a player option for $30.8 million next season.

articles.headline: Vikings to start reacquired QB Kirk Cousins vs. Packers
articles.description: Coach Kevin O'Connell called Kirk Cousins' ability to get reacquainted with the Vikings' offense "impressive."
articles.body:
EAGAN, Minn. -- Although there wasn't much question about it, Minnesota Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell confirmed Friday that quarterback Kirk Cousins will start Sunday against the Green Bay Packers, five days after the Vikings reacquired him from the Las Vegas Raiders at the trade deadline.

"I can't give him enough credit for coming in here and how he's gone about the week," O'Connell said, "both him and the coaching staff, getting him ready to go, working extremely hard, using all the time we possibly can. It's been really impressive what he's been able to do, and just the command and getting right back in the huddle with a lot of guys he's played with but certainly some guys he hasn't. It's been something that everybody has been very, very impressed with."

In the immediate aftermath of the trade, O'Connell had stopped short of naming Cousins his starter for Sunday, saying he wanted to make sure the veteran felt comfortable with the quick turnaround. The two spent much of Wednesday morning together, working through a playbook that Cousins first learned when the Vikings hired O'Connell in 2022. Since departing Minnesota after the 2023 season, Cousins has played for both the Raiders and the Atlanta Falcons. He had only two practices this week with the Vikings, on Thursday and Friday, but O'Connell saw no red flags.

"It's something we've always known about him," O'Connell said, "but the way he threw the football this week was just a really cool thing to see."

Cousins, however, won't have his full complement of pass catchers to work with Sunday. Tight end T.J. Hockenson won't play because of wrist and chest injuries suffered in Monday night's 23-6 loss to the Buffalo Bills. Wide receiver Jordan Addison, meanwhile, was added to the injury report Friday because of a thumb injury suffered in practice. The Vikings listed him as questionable.

Two other starters, linebacker Blake Cashman (concussion) and defensive lineman Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins (ankle), were also ruled out.

articles.body:
The NBA's leaguewide buzz never stops. 

The LeBron James and Jaylen Brown era with the Philadelphia 76ers got off to an ideal start by spoiling ring night for the New York Knicks. The Detroit Pistons also returned to their regular-season dominance with a win over the Boston Celtics, and the Oklahoma City Thunder struck the first rivalry blow against the San Antonio Spurs this season.

Now, what will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first season away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their impact this season?

All season, bookmark this page for the latest news and reactions from ESPN's NBA insiders.

Quick links:

Free agency grades | Trade grades

Transactions | Offseason buzz

ESPN's new NBA Trade Lab: Swing a deal!

Nov. 13

Murray, Pelicans working toward trade

New Orleans Pelicans guard Dejounte Murray wants a trade from the franchise, and his agent, Klutch Sports CEO Rich Paul, and team officials have started working on a resolution, sources tell ESPN's Shams Charania.

Murray has made it clear he is ready to play a key role in meaningful basketball elsewhere. The Pelicans are 4-8 to start the season and have lost four games in a row, including a 145-111 blowout at home to the Brooklyn Nets on Wednesday.

From Bobby Marks: Murray signed a four-year $114 million extension with Atlanta in July 2023 but was traded the following offseason to New Orleans. He has two years remaining on his contract -- $32.8 and $30.8 million, respectively, with a player option in the second year.

One salary-cap nugget a team interested in Murray will have to consider is the $2.4 million in unlikely bonuses. While he did not reach any of the incentives in the previous season, unlikely bonuses are applied to the first and second apron. With Murray on their books, New Orleans is $4 million below the luxury tax and $5.7 million under the first apron hard cap.

Despite five players (including the $44.9 million nonguaranteed contract of Zion Williamson) earning more than $21 million in 2027-28, New Orleans is well positioned below the luxury tax and apron.

After not having a first-round pick in the 2026 draft, New Orleans could have two picks in the top four in 2027 -- its own and Milwaukee's. If one of those picks falls between Nos. 5 and 30, the least favorable would go to Atlanta.

They close with the Cleveland Cavaliers' big response after a slow start and the Minnesota Timberwolves' impressive play without Anthony Edwards.

articles.headline: Fantasy hoops managers are giving up on Mikal Bridges, here's why you shouldn't
articles.description: Andre explains why Mikal Bridges continues to hold fantasy value despite the poor start to his season.
articles.headlineJa: ファンタジーバスケのオーナーたちがミカル・ブリッジズに見切りをつけ始めているが、諦めるべきではない理由
articles.descriptionJa: シーズン序盤の不調にもかかわらず、なぜミカル・ブリッジズがファンタジーでの価値を持ち続けているのか、アンドレが解説する。
articles.body:
Mikal Bridges is off to an objectively bad start to the season from a fantasy basketball perspective. Bad enough that I've been called out on social media for having him so high in my early season rankings.

Through his first 10 games this season, Bridges averaged 6.3 PPG and 0.9 3PG on 32.9 FG%. His cold shooting is affecting his minutes, leading New York Knicks coach Mike Brown to sit Bridges in the fourth quarter and therefore limit him to only playing 25.1 MPG. His peripheral stats like rebounds, assists, steals and blocks are actually right on his norms on a per-minute basis, but his reduced minutes have led to lower totals there as well.

Production-wise, this was Bridges' worst 10-game regular season stretch since March of this year, when he averaged 8.4 PPG and 1.0 3PG on 35.5 FG%. In fact, extended cold scoring spells aren't unusual for Bridges if you look at his career. Sometimes his shot just won't go in. But when the slump is over, Bridges has always returned to his typical high-level self. Last season, that 10-game stretch was swallowed by his other 72 games. All told, Bridges averaged 14.4 PPG on 49.0 FG% for the season that, along with his other stats, led to him finishing top 30 in the league in fantasy points as well as in the ESPN Player Rater.

And that's the point.

While Bridges' shot can be inconsistent, his production over the long haul is metronomic. He plays every game ... period. He has played in all 648 games in his nine-year career, never missing a single game. In the 2022-23 season Bridges was traded in the middle of the campaign, so he actually played 83 regular season games that year. But in an NBA full of injuries and load management, Bridges' iron-man durability is a super power.

Another of his fantasy super powers is the versatility of his game. Bridges is a 3-and-D player who contributes a bit to every category. Those contributions add up in both category leagues and points leagues, to the point that he always ends up among the top 30 in fantasy production. And the consistency has been across roles and teams, as well. In his last four full seasons leading up to this one, he split a season between being a role player for the Phoenix Suns and the primary scorer for the Brooklyn Nets in 2022-23, was a primary scorer for the Nets (23-24), and then was back to a role player with the Knicks since 2024-25 -- and his fantasy points (both totals and per game) end up roughly the same every year.

He always ends up at the same spot.

Always?

Bridges' incredibly slow start this season rightfully raises some questions. After having him in my preseason top-40 fantasy rankings, Bridges has slid outside the top 80 in this week's rankings update. The rankings factor in feedback from the current season, and Bridges' fantasy average is just far below his norm.

But, again, a closer look shows that only one aspect of Bridges' game is out of whack right now: his shooting, which is directly affecting his scoring and minutes played.

articles.headline: Borussia Dortmund to end controversial sponsorship with arms manufacturer
articles.description: Borussia Dortmund says it won't renew a sponsorship deal with Germany's largest arms manufacturer Rheinmetall, which drew criticism from fans.
articles.body:
Borussia Dortmund says it won't renew a sponsorship deal with Germany's largest arms manufacturer Rheinmetall, which drew criticism from fans as soon as it was signed.

The official sponsorship agreement between the German club and Rheinmetall, which has been in place since 2024, expires on June, 30, 2027.

- Dortmund fans use dummy tank to protest arms-maker deal

Club chairman Carsten Cramer said in an interview published on the club's website Friday that members had voted at the 2024 annual general meeting on a motion not to extend the partnership deal beyond 2027.

"Naturally, we took that into account in our discussions with Rheinmetall and treated it seriously," he said. "We are, of course, aware that our partnership has been controversial from the outset."

When the deal was signed, German media reported it was worth up to €9 million ($10 million) per year.

"From summer 2027, we will lose the income from the sponsorship agreement," Cramer said. "That is a fact. It reduces our financial room for manoeuvre. We will have to reprioritize planned investments and carefully examine how we can find viable solutions."

Rheinmetall is a "champion partner" and Dortmund displays the company's banner on advertising hoardings during games.

The agreement has caused friction among supporters to varying degrees, with some Dortmund fans even going so far as to renounce their support.

Founded in 1889 as "Rheinische Metallwaaren- und Maschinenfabrik Actiengesellschaft," Rheinmetall was one of Germany's biggest armaments manufacturers during both World Wars. It made use of forced labor during World War II.

articles.headline: Recap: USMNT's Pochettino in tears as he agrees to join Man United
articles.description: USMNT head coach Mauricio Pochettino is leaving to join Manchester United. Read all the news, analysis and reaction from ESPN.
articles.body:
United States men's national team head coach Mauricio Pochettino will leave his post and become Manchester United manager, it was announced on Friday.

Just over 24 hours after United sacked Michael Carrick, the club already has a new manager on the way. Pochettino will manage the USMNT's upcoming Concacaf Nations League games against Haiti, and his first game in charge at United will be at arch-rivals Liverpool on Nov. 22.

It means Pochettino, who has previously enjoyed coaching spells at Tottenham Hotspur, Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea, is back in the Premier League.

Read all the news, analysis and reaction from ESPN.

articles.headline: 10 Best: Ranking the world's top men's soccer players ... again!
articles.description: Who is the best soccer player in the world at the November international break? ESPN's latest rankings are here.
articles.body:
For as much as I make fun of the Ballon d'Or process and how ridiculous the mushy, vague, contradictory criteria are, I think they've probably gotten it right in each of the past three years. At least, they haven't gotten it wrong.

When I wrote up my theoretical ballots in each of the past three years, my three choices were Rodri, Ousmane Dembélé and Harry Kane -- the three eventual winners. Once you move beyond the top pick, though, things start to get really weird. Imagine watching the 2025-26 Premier League season and then finding out that Chelsea's Marc Cucurella got more Ballon d'Or votes than Arsenal's Gabriel Magalhães and William Saliba -- combined.

Since the award tends to identify one of the best players on one of the best teams in the world, it does tend to identify a worthy winner. But it rarely identifies any other worthy winners.

Remember when Mohamed Salah led the Premier League in goals and assists two seasons ago for a dominant Liverpool team? He finished fourth, with a vote total closer to 30th than first.

Who, then, is the best player in the world right now? Or rather, who are the best players in the world right now?

In August, we launched the 10 Best List, a recurring look at who I'd estimate to be the -- you got it -- 10 best soccer players in the world. We're back, post-Harry Kane Ballon d'Or, to update the list.

As a reminder, I'm using this as my guidance: "If you added this player to an average round-of-16 Champions League team, how much more likely would the team be to win the tournament?" And if a player is injured or has been injured recently, I'm dropping him out of the top 10.

All right, let's get to the list.

10. Vitinha, midfielder, Paris Saint-Germain

Previous rank: Unranked

Because of the injury rule I made up, we've had to drop Dembélé (No. 1) and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia (No. 3) from the list. The former hasn't played since before Halloween, while the latter is out for the season with a torn ACL. And yet it seems like PSG remain the best soccer team in the world without either of them.

Last year, Arsenal finished the league phase of the UEFA Champions League with 23 goals, more than anyone else. PSG currently have 20 goals -- through four Champions League games, two of which were against Manchester City and Barcelona.

So, they have to have someone on the list. I don't think Vitinha would be a controversial pick here for pretty much anyone other than a guy who published a book that devotes an entire chapter to the issues with evaluating, measuring and valuing midfield play. But that guy also happens to be writing this article.

There are two ways to really impact the game as a midfielder: contribute goals and assists while also doing the normal, expected amount of midfielder stuff ... or do an incredible, outlier amount of the midfielder stuff.
